clue.text: Teller was lax with cash, restricting transactions in financial meltdown

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the shuffled letters close around the abbreviation
lax means slack or loose, so these letters are loosened into a new order

parts.note: TR is a standard abbreviation for transaction(s)

explanation.surface: A careless bank cashier handling money sloppily gets blamed for a collapse of the markets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teller' and 'cash' set a banking scene, but 'lax' is the anagram signal and 'restricting' the container; 'with' only joins the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1929 collapse of share prices on the New York exchange is the classic example of a financial meltdown.

clue.text: Tackle giving Champion victory at outset

indicators.note: at outset places the victory word at the start, ahead of the champion abbreviation

parts.note: a victory is a win
CH is the abbreviation for champion, as at dog shows

explanation.surface: A sports commentator says a big tackle gave the champion an early win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a sports move, but here it is lifting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle in the sense of hoisting gear covers ropes, pulleys and a crank-driven drum for hauling loads.

clue.text: Legislation error precludes fine

indicators.note: precludes means shuts out, so the fine abbreviation is excluded from the word for error

parts.note: an error is a flaw
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A mistake in the drafting rules out a penalty under the new statute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty, which suits the legal surface, but only gives the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: Legislation is the body of statutes passed by a parliament, the rules people must obey.

clue.text: Cave feature sat with tactile rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A caver sat touching the textured rock formations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' seems to belong to the cave scene but signals the rearrangement of SAT and TACTILE; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral spike hanging from a cavern ceiling, formed by dripping water, is a typical cave feature.

clue.text: A portion's nasty (to vermin, that is)

definitions.text: A portion's nasty (to vermin, that is)

indicators.note: nasty suggests something turned bad, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe-s is kept as an S for the letter pool

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a serving tastes horrible, but only for rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the rearrangement of A PORTIONS and a description of the answer: a serving that is harmful to vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: Poisoned bait laid out for rats is a helping of food that is deadly to vermin specifically.

clue.text: Resin the Spanish send out, losing little time

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so the time abbreviation is removed from the word for send out

parts.note: to send out is to emit
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Spaniard exports a resin but cuts the delivery time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little time' gives the single letter T, a short form of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic gum from tropical trees, used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Eccentric vehicle heading for ditch

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An erratic motor is heading off the road into a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like it describes the vehicle, but it is the definition, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is old slang for an amusing oddball, a person with quirky behaviour.

clue.text: Classic drama meeting audience requirements?

definitions.meaning: a Shakespeare comedy set in the Forest of Arden
doing things just the way the spectators want them

explanation.surface: A classic play is staged to please the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Shakespeare's comedy also reads as a phrase for giving people exactly what they want.

clue.text: Sound mostly delivering shivers imperfectly

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: sound in the sense of healthy is hale
something tingly sends prickles or shivers through you

explanation.surface: A speaker's sound shakes imperfectly as they deliver their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise but means healthy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with stops and hesitations means doing it falteringly, not perfectly.

clue.text: Replacement actors taking on the French city

parts.note: a replacement is a new one
the actors in a production are its cast
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A theatre brings in understudies to play a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A major city in the north-east of England on the River Tyne.

clue.text: Wager gold will be brought back for a king

indicators.note: brought back means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: lay as a noun or verb means a bet
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A bet of gold will be returned to its owner, a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit for a king belongs to or befits a monarch, the adjective for the crown.

clue.text: Causing sleep in chap going out around end of day

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters wrap round a letter
out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged
end of means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A man heading out at nightfall makes you drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' reads as leaving, but 'going' is fodder and 'out' signals the anagram; 'around' wraps the shuffle round the end of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the drowsy state on the verge of slumber, or anything inducing it.

clue.text: Thinking person's setter hopes vaguely to block cry of woe?

parts.note: PHI is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter

indicators.note: to block means to sit inside and stop up the cry

parts.note: lor, short for lord, is a dated exclamation of dismay

indicators.note: vaguely means indistinctly arranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A deep thinker's setter hopes in a vague way to stop a wail of grief.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'person' is a link meaning has; 'vaguely' signals the anagram and 'to block' the insertion. Phi is the setter's own pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinker devoted to reasoning about knowledge and existence is a scholar of wisdom.

clue.text: Muslim provided reduced employment after setback

indicators.note: a setback is a turning back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: provided means if, as a condition

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: employment in the sense of using something is use

explanation.surface: A Muslim worker finds hours cut after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts the last letter of the employment word, and 'after setback' turns the whole pair round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi is a follower of Islamic mysticism, so is a Muslim.

clue.text: Historic prison child, one growing slowly

parts.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A child in an old prison camp grows up slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising mineral column builds up from the cave floor over centuries as drips deposit calcite.

clue.text: Young married possibly mostly in the right, not initially likely to be wrong

indicators.note: to be wrong means the letters are set in the wrong order, so rearranged
not means without, so the following letter is removed from the pool
initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A young married couple are mostly right, and unlikely to be wrong at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L ('initially likely') from MOSTLY IN THE RIGHT, and 'to be wrong' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Young marrieds are often in their thirties; the term describes that age group, also from a TV drama.

clue.text: Will try to agree over opening of treaty

parts.note: to try is to test
amen is said to express agreement

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Diplomats will try to agree on the start of a treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the future tense but is the definition, the legal document; 'over' is a link in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the document setting out what happens to someone's estate.

clue.text: It shows up in a variety of roaming?

definitions.text: It shows up in a variety of roaming?

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the rearranged letters
a variety of suggests a different arrangement, so these letters are rearranged
shows up in a down clue means the word rises, read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Something appears in some form of wandering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows up' turns 'It' upwards in this down clue, and 'a variety of' signals the anagram; the whole clue also describes the answer as a kind of roaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal travel by birds or herds is a type of wandering from place to place.

clue.text: Making film largely misjudged for target spot?

parts.note: making a film is shooting it

indicators.note: misjudged means got wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film shoot largely misjudged its choice of location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' looks like 'mostly' trimming a word, but it is the fodder rearranged by 'misjudged'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground stall or range where people fire at targets is a spot for aiming.

clue.text: Quantity of nerve recalled in no Times article

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about courage is withdrawn from the Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: The long fibre of a nerve cell carrying impulses is one part of the body's wiring.

clue.text: Genuine launch trajectory?

definitions.meaning: honest, not lying, as in telling it as it is
a rocket's path that goes vertically into the sky

explanation.surface: A real rocket path is under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means honestly, and literally describes something rising vertically.

clue.text: Sum? US city child's given up

parts.note: a tot is a small child; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: given up in a down clue means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A child in an American city has given up on arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' looks like surrender, but in a down clue it turns LA upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition result is the overall figure, which a sum produces.

clue.text: Entertainment soon to appear, or long over?

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A show coming up soon, or one that ended long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue was published before Christmas, when pantomime season, a British family theatre tradition, was approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is a comic family stage show, a seasonal entertainment around Christmas in Britain.

clue.text: Pieces not allowed in Asian country: this song?

indicators.note: not allowed in means shut out, so the pieces are removed

parts.note: Armenia is a country in the Caucasus, counted as part of Asia
chessmen are pieces, so men

explanation.surface: A song is banned in an Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' looks like musical pieces but means chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo melody is a song; the result of the subtraction is offered as this song.

clue.text: Soporific expression of sympathy finally put forward

indicators.note: the final letter is moved forward to the start

parts.note: there, there is said to comfort someone

explanation.surface: A sympathetic murmur finally sends someone off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: This anaesthetic gas was once used to knock patients unconscious, so it induces sleep.

clue.text: Husband engaged in test, shifting a 1 ton mass of stones

indicators.note: shifting means removing, so the letter a is taken away

parts.note: a test is a trial
the figure 1 stands for the letter I

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A husband is put through a test, shifting a one-ton mass of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' here means taking away the letter A, not moving it; 'engaged in' then puts the husband's H into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric structure of two uprights topped by a lintel, as at Stonehenge, is a structure of stone blocks.

clue.text: Tool not left in excavation

indicators.note: not means without, so the left abbreviation is removed

parts.note: an excavation is a hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A tool was not left in the dig site.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled garden implement with a blade for weeding is a tool.

clue.text: Pointedly ignore performance: Neil — boy with date — getting busy!

parts.note: a turn is a performance by a variety act

indicators.note: getting busy suggests agitated activity, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage act where Neil, a lad and a date get frisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberately overlook something you know about is to ignore it on purpose, as Nelson did with his telescope.
